subject: math

entries: Arc length and sector area: a 60 degree sector is 60/360 = 1/6 of the circle, so the arc is 1/6 of 2 pi r and the sector area is 1/6 of pi r squared.
slots.label: Arc length and sector area
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Pyramid volume, revealed: pouring the pyramid into the matching prism takes three full pyramids, so the volume is 1/3 x base area x height.
slots.label: Pyramid volume, revealed
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Sphere volume: stacking thin disk slices of the sphere gives 4/3 pi r cubed; for r = 3 cm that is 36 pi, about 113 cubic centimetres.
slots.label: Sphere volume
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: doubling r doubles area: growing r from 3 cm to 6 cm fits four small disks inside the big one, so the area goes from 9 pi to 36 pi.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The length of a curve along a circle: the angle-over-360 fraction of the full circumference 2 pi r.
slots.label: Arc length
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A slice of a circle bounded by two radii and an arc; its area is the angle-over-360 fraction of pi r squared.
slots.label: Sector
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: One third of base area times vertical height: three identical pyramids fill the prism on the same base with the same height.
slots.label: Pyramid volume
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A perfectly round solid where every surface point is the radius r from the centre; its volume is 4/3 pi r cubed.
slots.label: Sphere
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The multiplier on lengths when a shape grows; areas multiply by its square and volumes by its cube.
slots.label: Scale factor
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
